title: Brain surgery
what: Through an opening in the skull, a neurosurgeon removes a tumor or other growth. The work is done under a microscope, protecting healthy areas.
why: For brain tumors, some bleeds, aneurysms, and other conditions that need surgery.
duration: surgery usually takes several hours, with 5 to 10 days in hospital, sometimes longer
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
What has changed: speech, vision, weakness, memory

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually an MRI, blood tests, an ECG, and checkups by a GP and other doctors. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Sometimes a small area is shaved. Ask if you need to do anything in advance.

prepare.title: Family
prepare.text: Agree on who will keep in touch with the doctor and help after discharge.

bring: MRI and CT images on a disc
steps: You change, and IV lines are placed
Your head is held still in a special frame
The surgeon opens a small area of the skull
The growth is removed under a microscope
The bone is put back, and the skin is stitched
After surgery, you are watched in intensive care or a high-dependency unit
feel: Headache and facial swelling. You will get painkillers
Weakness and sleepiness in the first days
Sometimes speech, vision, or arm strength changes for a while. Your doctor will explain
after: The first day is usually in intensive care, under close watch
You start getting up gradually, as your doctor allows
Stitches usually come out after 7 to 14 days
The lab results will guide further treatment
Drive only after your doctor allows it
red_flags: A seizure or loss of consciousness: call emergency services
A sudden severe headache, vomiting, or confusion: call emergency services
New weakness in an arm or leg, or trouble speaking: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or discharge from the wound

faq.a: The brain itself feels no pain. The skin and muscles of the head hurt, and painkillers relieve it.

faq.q: Can the surgery be done while I am awake?
faq.a: Sometimes, if the tumor is near the areas for speech or movement. The surgeon decides.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Bring your scans on a disc and your medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
